```{r import data, include=FALSE}
# Import Pitnacree flow data directly from ZIP file in Github
pitnacree <- read.csv(unz("pitnacree.zip", "pitnacree.csv"))

pitnacree <- pitnacree %>%
  mutate(Timestamp = parse_date_time(Timestamp, orders = c("ymd HMS", "ymd HM", "ymd"), tz = "UTC"))

raw <- pitnacree$Timestamp
 bad <- raw[is.na(ymd_hms(raw, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE))]
 head(bad); length(bad)
```


### Importing Peaks ###
```{r peaks}
threshold     <- 260  # Peaks over threshold (m3/s), change for initial threshold
steps_per_day <- 96   # 15-minute data resolution (24 * 4)

# Put Pitnacree on a continuous 15-minute grid
pit <- tibble(
  Timestamp = seq(
    min(pitnacree$Timestamp, na.rm= TRUE),
    max(pitnacree$Timestamp, na.rm=TRUE),
    by = "15 min"
  )
) %>%
  left_join(
    pitnacree %>% dplyr::select(Timestamp, Value),
    by = "Timestamp"
  )

flow <- pit$Value
flow_noNA <- replace_na(flow, 0) # 0 ensures peak detection ignores missing intervals


# Extract candidate peaks exceeding the specified threshold
raw <- findpeaks(flow_noNA, minpeakheight = threshold, minpeakdistance = 1, zero = "0")

cand <- tibble(
  max_flow   = raw[, 1],
  max_time   = raw[, 2],
  peak_begin = raw[, 3],
  peak_end   = raw[, 4]
) %>%
  arrange(max_time) %>%
  mutate(ttr = max_time - peak_begin) # Time to rise in 15-min steps


# Compute average time to peak from "clean" isolated events
near_other <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cand)), function(i) {
  any(abs(cand$max_time[-i] - cand$max_time[i]) < 7 * steps_per_day)
})

clean <- cand %>%
  mutate(clean = flow[peak_begin] < 0.5 * max_flow & !near_other & !is.na(flow[peak_begin]))

avg_ttr <- mean(clean$ttr[clean$clean])
min_sep <- 3 * avg_ttr
cat(sprintf("Avg time to peak: %.2f hours | Min FEH separation: %.2f hours\n", avg_ttr / 4, min_sep / 4))


# Filter candidate peaks using FEH independence criteria 
keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(cand))
last <- 1

for (k in 2:nrow(cand)) {
  sep <- cand$max_time[k] - cand$max_time[last]
  independent <- sep >= min_sep
  
  if (independent) {
    trough <- min(flow[cand$max_time[last]:cand$max_time[k]], na.rm = TRUE)
    independent <- trough < (2/3) * cand$max_flow[last]
  }
  
  if (independent) {
    last <- k
  } else if (cand$max_flow[k] > cand$max_flow[last]) {
    keep[last] <- FALSE
    last <- k
  } else {
    keep[k] <- FALSE
  }
}

peaks_passed <- cand[keep, ]
n_years <- sum(!is.na(flow)) / (steps_per_day * 365.25)
```

## Emma D


```{r scale peaks to same grid, normalise}
K    <- 101                          # grid points per hydrograph
grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = K)

resample_event <- function(i) {
  idx <- peaks_passed$peak_begin[i]:peaks_passed$peak_end[i]
  x   <- (seq_along(idx) - 1) / (length(idx) - 1)   # time / width, in [0,1]
  approx(x, pit$Value[idx], xout = grid)$y               # linearly interpolate to grid
}

H <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(peaks_passed)), resample_event)   # K x n matrix
width <- peaks_passed$peak_end - peaks_passed$peak_begin   #keep the widths as suggested
pk    <- peaks_passed$max_flow

H_norm_p    <- sweep(H, 2, pk, "/")                        # try normalising by peak?

```


```{r linear fit}
deg <- 8 #just for a decent approx, will need to try a few and measure reconstruction error before choosing one
B   <- poly(grid, deg)               # orthogonal polynomial basis, same for all events

fit   <- lm(H_norm_p ~ B)                  # matrix response with one regression per event
coefs <- t(coef(fit))                # n x (deg+1): intercept + deg coefficients

#reconstruciton
Hhat <- cbind(1, B) %*% t(coefs)     # K x n fitted hydrographs

#see approximated hydrograph vs real
matplot(grid, cbind(H_norm_p[, 6], Hhat[, 6]), type = "l")
```


## Harry


```{r harry}
# 1. Hydrograph matrix: one row per event, hourly values from 72h before to 72h after the peak,
#    divided by the peak flow so each row is a shape
pk_idx <- sort(peaks_passed$max_time)
get_window <- function(i) {
  lo <- i - 72 * 4;  hi <- i + 72 * 4
  if (lo < 1 || hi > length(flow)) return(NULL)
  seg <- flow[lo:hi]
  if (mean(is.na(seg)) > 0.05) return(NULL)
  seg <- approx(seq_along(seg), seg, xout = seq_along(seg), rule = 2)$y
  seg[seq(1, length(seg), by = 4)] / seg[289]
}
segs <- lapply(pk_idx, get_window)
Y <- do.call(rbind, segs[!sapply(segs, is.null)])
t_h <- -72:72
dim(Y)

# 2. PCA (centre, don't scale: all columns already on the same scale)
pca_result <- prcomp(Y, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)

# 3. Variance explained
plot(pca_result)
head(cumsum(pca_result$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result$sdev^2), 10)

# 4. Loadings as a function of time
plot(t_h, pca_result$rotation[, 1], type = "l", col = "red", ylim = range(pca_result$rotation[, 1:2]),
     xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Loading", main = "Loadings for PC1 and PC2")
lines(t_h, pca_result$rotation[, 2], col = "blue")
legend("bottomright", legend = c("PC1", "PC2"), col = c("red", "blue"), lty = 1)

# 5. Scores
head(pca_result$x[, 1:3])

# 6. Reconstruct hydrograph 1 using k PCs
mean_hydro <- colMeans(Y)
k <- 3
recon <- mean_hydro + pca_result$x[1, 1:k] %*% t(pca_result$rotation[, 1:k])
plot(t_h, Y[1, ], type = "l", lwd = 2, xlab = "Hours from peak", ylab = "Q / Qmax",
     main = "Original vs PCA reconstruction (hydrograph 1)")
lines(t_h, recon, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Original", "Recon"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2)
```

```{r checks}
# Check for missing or duplicate data
sum(is.na(pitnacree$Timestamp))
sum(duplicated(pitnacree$Timestamp))
sum(is.na(pitnacree$Value))

# Check the number of extracted peaks
nrow(cand)
nrow(peaks_passed)

# Check the number of hydrographs used in PCA
nrow(Y)

# Calculate duration of each extracted event (hours)
duration <- (peaks_passed$peak_end -
             peaks_passed$peak_begin) / 4

# Summary statistics
summary(duration)

# Distribution of event durations
hist(duration,
     breaks = 30,
     main = "Distribution of extracted event durations",
     xlab = "Duration (hours)",
     col = "lightblue")

```

```{r checks2}
end <- peaks_passed$peak_end[i]

hi <- min(length(flow), peak + 72 * 4)

     type = "l",
     xlab = "Time",
     ylab = "Flow (m3/s)",
     main = "Flood hydrograph with extracted boundaries")

abline(v = pit$Timestamp[start], col = "blue", lty = 2)
abline(v = pit$Timestamp[end], col = "red", lty = 2)

# Mark the maximum

legend("topright",
       legend = c("Flow", "Start", "End", "Peak"),
       col = c("black", "blue", "red", "darkgreen"),
       lty = c(1, 2, 2, 2))

```

```{r checks3}
# Identify hydrographs retained for PCA
valid <- which(!sapply(segs, is.null))

# Find maximum normalised flow for each hydrograph
max_ratio <- apply(Y, 1, max)

# Find the time of the largest peak in each window
max_hour <- t_h[max.col(Y, ties.method = "first")]

# Create table of potentially problematic events
problem_events <- tibble(
  Event = valid,
  Date = pit$Timestamp[peaks_passed$max_time[valid]],
  Selected_peak = peaks_passed$max_flow[valid],
  Ratio = max_ratio,
  Hours_to_max = max_hour
) %>%
  filter(Ratio > 1.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(Ratio))

# Display the 27 cases
print(n=27, head(problem_events, 27))

```
